name: Agent Zero
vibe_summary: Agent Zero gives your agent a full Dockerized Linux desktop with GUI apps, browser DOM annotation, and live document coworking. It's a mature, heavily-featured open agent framework with a thriving plugin hub and multi-agent delegation.
best_for: Users who want an agent with a full GUI Linux desktop
Developers needing browser automation with DOM annotation
Teams wanting per-project isolation of files, secrets, and memory
avoid_if: You need a lightweight or edge-deployable agent
You cannot run Docker on your machine
You want minimal shell-access risk without hardening
You need a managed, zero-setup cloud service

overview_markdown:
Agent Zero is an open agent framework built around the idea of giving an LLM agent a complete computer: a Dockerized Linux desktop (XFCE via Xpra), a browser with DOM annotation, live document coworking for Markdown/Writer/Spreadsheet/Presentation files, and a host-machine bridge via the A0 CLI. It supports projects with isolated files, secrets, memories, and model presets, plus multi-agent cooperation where agents delegate research, coding, or review tasks to focused subagents through a unified, persisted child-context lifecycle.

Architecturally it is Python-based and runs anywhere Docker runs, from a Raspberry Pi or cheap VPS to a GPU server, with a guided A0 Launcher desktop app for setup. Its Plugin Hub offers 100+ community extensions, and internals (prompts, tools, skills, settings) are transparent and editable. Recent commits show active hardening work: pinned Docker desktop package versions, authenticated and path-traversal-safe WebUI asset routes, scoped plugin cache invalidation, and backup restore origin fixes.

Compared to OpenClaw, Agent Zero trades lightweight multi-channel messaging for deep computer-use capability: it excels at GUI automation, document collaboration, and extensibility, but carries a heavier resource footprint and a larger shell-access risk surface that operators must sandbox deliberately.
